summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as the DHCP server on the private eth1 network shared with node2 and node3. Added a UCI network interface 'priv' (192.168.50.1/24 on eth1), a firewall zone 'priv' (input/output/forward ACCEPT) with forwarding to wan, and a dnsmasq DHCP pool (192.168.50.100-249) on that interface. Added a static DHCP host reservation binding node2's eth1 MAC to 192.168.50.50, so node2 always gets that same address; node3 is left unreserved and draws from the general pool. Verified node2 gets 192.168.50.50 across repeated lease renewals and node3 gets a distinct pool address. Made the DHCP-client config persistent on node2/node3 (Alpine /etc/network/interfaces + rc-update). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3: captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/service baselines, issued native `reboot`, polled until exec access returned, confirmed each node's boot_id changed and uptime reset to ~0, and verified post-restart recovery (node1's dnsmasq/firewall/priv-interface config and lease table intact; node2 auto-reacquired its reserved 192.168.50.50; node3 auto-reacquired a pool address).
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network state and identified eth1 as the unconfigured private network segment
Configured UCI network interface 'priv' (192.168.50.1/24) on node1's eth1
Added firewall zone 'priv' with input/output/forward ACCEPT and forwarding to wan
Configured dnsmasq DHCP pool (start=100,limit=150) on the 'priv' interface
Added a static DHCP host reservation for node2's eth1 MAC -> 192.168.50.50
Brought up eth1 as a DHCP client on node2 and node3 and verified addressing
Made eth1 DHCP-client config persistent via /etc/network/interfaces and rc-update on node2/node3
Verified node2 receives the same reserved IP across repeated udhcpc renewals while node3 draws from the general pool
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/service-health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1, polled until exec access returned, verified changed boot_id and recovered dnsmasq/firewall/network config and lease table
Restarted node2, verified changed boot_id and automatic reacquisition of reserved 192.168.50.50
Restarted node3, verified changed boot_id and automatic reacquisition of a general-pool address distinct from node2's

evidence.requirement: node1 hands out addresses on the shared private network (eth1)
evidence.summary: Configured static IP 192.168.50.1/24 on node1 eth1, firewall zone 'priv', and dnsmasq DHCP server (pool 100-150) on that interface

evidence.requirement: node2 always receives the same address across repeated leases
evidence.summary: Static host reservation binds node2's eth1 MAC to 192.168.50.50; repeated udhcpc renewals (including after node1's restart) all returned 192.168.50.50

evidence.requirement: node3 is addressed from the general pool (not a fixed reservation)
evidence.summary: node3 received 192.168.50.190 from the dynamic pool, distinct from node2's reserved address, confirmed in node1's lease table

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id df9617f9...; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); post-restart boot_id 9961e960... (changed), uptime reset to 0 min; dnsmasq/network running, priv interface/firewall/dhcp config intact, node2 lease still tracked

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f8fd73b7...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 25ca6fb1... (changed), uptime reset to 0 min; eth1 automatically re-acquired reserved address 192.168.50.50 on boot, confirmed in node1 lease table

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 75b74cf0...; reboot ack (exec stream closed); post-restart boot_id 9889bcc1... (changed), uptime reset to 0 min; eth1 automatically re-acquired a general-pool address 192.168.50.190 on boot, confirmed in node1 lease table
